title: Falcons QB battle: Michael Penix Jr. making push against Tua Tagovailoa - CBS Sports
description: Sources say Penix's "live arm" is already turning heads as the quarterback competition in Atlanta officially kick
body:
Sources say Penix's "live arm" is already turning heads as the quarterback competition in Atlanta officially kicks into high gear
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Aug 23, 2026
                            
                    at
    12:09 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            2 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        Even while limited to just 7-on-7 sessions and individual drills in recent months, there were still moments from Michael Penix Jr. in practice when the 2024 top-10 draft pick was able to stand out and impress the new Atlanta Falcons staff thanks to a certain part of his skill set: a left arm that's capable of delivering throws that many other NFL quarterbacks, including the others in Atlanta, aren't capable of making."Some of the balls that jump out of his hand," a source said, "and that kind of live arm, it's impressive to see." That arm is part of the reason that it will now become an interesting next three weeks in Atlanta leading into the Falcons' regular season opener against the Steelers on Sept. 13.With Penix -- who has been working from a November ACL injury -- being cleared to fully participate in practice starting Monday, the Falcons are of the mindset that their QB competition can now truly begin.
While it's fair to say that free agent signee Tua Tagovailoa remains the favorite to win Atlanta's starting QB job, Penix will now get a chance these next few weeks to try and prove that he's the better option."It's just a true evaluation now with both guys being able to be in the huddle, control the line of scrimmage and control the game flow," a source said. "You're able to get a real sense from that aspect now and who's able to bring this offense to life."Penix made nine starts last season before suffering the ACL injury, which was the fifth season-ending injury he's suffered since the start of his college career, including the third ACL tear.
Among the good from those nine starts was a touchdown-to-interception ratio of nine-to-three, two games with at least 298 passing yards and a three-touchdown performance vs. the Patriots. Among the bad: A 3-5 record for the Falcons in the games Penix played from start to finish, a completion percentage (60.1) that ranked fourth-worst among NFL QBs that made at least eight starts and a QB rating of 88.5 that tied, coincidentally with Tagovailoa, for just 26th-best in the NFL.However, Penix will now get his chance to fully show what he can do under Atlanta's new staff and new head coach Kevin Stefanski. Although sources have emphasized that Penix has already done a lot during his work in 7-on-7 and individual drills, the team's practice Monday will give this staff their first look at him in an 11-on-11 setting.The timing is good for the Falcons. While a source said that Tagovailoa "has grown, especially (transitioning) from what he was asked to do in Miami and what he's asked to do now," there have also been ups and downs for him this offseason. That includes during the Falcons' preseason opener vs. the Broncos when he was 3 of 5 for 22 yards.
As part of Atlanta's plan, Tagovailoa didn't play in Atlanta's second preseason game but is expected to play in the preseason finale against the Dolphins on Friday. It's unclear as of yet whether Penix will play in that game.Either way, even if it's just during practice, the Falcons' staff will now get a real chance to evaluate and compare both quarterbacks and then make a determination regarding which is the better option to be the team's starting QB.That important part of this process starts Monday.

title: Ryan Weathers injury: Yankees starter lands on IL as rotation takes another hit - CBS Sports
description: Weathers said on Sunday that he doesn't believe the injury will end his season
body:
Weathers said on Sunday that he doesn't believe the injury will end his season
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Aug 23, 2026
                            
                    at
    11:48 am ET
                        
                •
            
            1 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        The New York Yankees' rotation has taken another hit. Mere days after losing Max Fried to a bone bruise in his pitching elbow, fellow lefty Ryan Weathers has landed on the injured list with a left forearm flexor strain. The Yankees have recalled right-hander Brendan Beck in a corresponding move. While Weathers doesn't yet have a clear timeline, on Sunday, he told reporters, including the Athletic, that tests have shown his elbow to be structurally sound and that he doesn't think the injury will necessarily put an end to his season. Weathers also said that a similar yet more severe injury last season cost him a month.Weathers will not throw for two to four weeks, manager Aaron Boone said on Sunday (via the New York Daily News), but has a "great chance" of pitching again this season, possibly as a reliever.The Yankees acquired Weathers, 26, in a trade this past offseason with the Marlins. He's been an effective and stabilizing presence in the New York rotation this season across 25 starts. 
The loss of Weathers leaves the Yankees with, at present, four healthy starting pitchers, and that includes the recently returned Carlos Rodón. As well, Will Warren, who may have been ticketed for the bullpen before Fried and Weathers went down, will now have to remain in the rotation. It remains to be seen how manager Aaron Boone will navigate this latest challenge as the Yankees attempt to catch the Rays at the top of the American League East standings or, failing that, retain the top wild-card spot in the AL. The Yankees have struggled to score runs for some time, and that's increased the stress upon and the importance of the pitching staff. The Yankees on Sunday did reinstate outfielder Cody Bellinger from the IL, which should help matters on that front. However, the rotation -- the bedrock in the Bronx all season -- is now a major concern. 
The Yankees enter play on Sunday with a record of 73-56, which puts them three games behind the Rays in the division.

title: Randy Arozarena becomes third in MLB history with first-pitch home run, walk-off homer -- just days after PCA - CBS Sports
description: Arozarena also robbed a home run in the Mariners' win over the Cubs on Saturday

Arozarena also robbed a home run in the Mariners' win over the Cubs on Saturday

    12:07 pm ET

        Mere days after Pete Crow-Armstrong of the Cubs became the second player to hit a first-pitch home run and a walk-off home run in the same game, Randy Arozarena of the Mariners became the third – coincidentally, at the expense of PCA's Cubs. 
Arozarena on Saturday hit the opening pitch of the bottom of the first – a sinker from David Peterson – 416 feet to center for a 1-0 Seattle lead and his 18th home run of the season. Much later, in the bottom of the ninth, Arozarena came up with two on, two out and the Mariners down by a pair of runs. Arozarena delivered in the hugest way with a game-winning blast off a Jacob Webb slider that, even more coincidentally, soared over the glove of PCA out in center and gave the hosts a crucial 5-4 win. This is to say nothing of Arozerena's home run robbery earlier in the game, which means his entire evening on the job merits a look: In all, Arozarena was 3 for 4 with a walk and those pair of homers, and all of it was essential to Seattle's thrilling win. The 31-year-old three-time All-Star is now slashing .275/.369/.463 on the season, which is good for an OPS+ of 139. Arozarena also leads the Mariners in WAR with a figure of 4.3.
"I think it's my biggest game," Arozarena said after the game through an interpreter (via MLB.com). "I didn't expect to come into the game and hit two home runs and rob one. But yes, it was a special day for me, a special performance for myself. But most importantly, this moment in time for the team and being able to help the team win is the biggest thing for today."For his bit of history, Arozarena is now just the seventh player since 1900 to hit a leadoff home run and a walk-off home run in the same game: PlayerDateOpponentRandy Arozarena, MarinersAug. 22, 2026 				CubsPete Crow-Armstrong, Cubs 				Aug. 17, 2026 				White Sox 				Chris Young, Diamondbacks 				Aug. 7, 2010 				Padres 				Ian Kinsler, Rangers 				July 19, 2009 				Twins 				Reed Johnson, Blue Jays 				June 15, 2003 				Cubs 				Darin Erstad, Angels 				June 25, 2000 				Twins 				Vic Power, KC Athletics 				May 7, 1957 				Orioles 				That he hit that leadoff home run on the first pitch puts him in even more exclusive company. As noted above, just PCA and Vic Power in 1957 had achieved that feat before Arozarena joined them on Saturday night in Seattle. 
Arozarena's heroics improved the Mariners to 62-68 on the season. While that's a disappointing record for the club that made it to the ALCS last year, they're also just three games behind the Astros in the AL West. They also remain in the chase for the third and final wild-card spot in the AL.

title: Missouri star RB Ahmad Hardy to miss opener, hasn't been cleared to practice as he recovers after being shot - CBS Sports
description: Hardy, the SEC's leading rusher last season, is still recovering after being wounded in an offseason shooting
body:
Hardy, the SEC's leading rusher last season, is still recovering after being wounded in an offseason shooting
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Aug 23, 2026
                            
                    at
    11:08 am ET
                        
                •
            
            2 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        Ahmad Hardy will not play in Missouri's season opener against Arkansas-Pine Bluff on Sept. 3 as the star running back continues his recovery from a gunshot wound suffered in May.Missouri coach Eli Drinkwitz announced Saturday night that Hardy has not progressed far enough to be ready for the opener. Hardy has been working through his rehabilitation during fall camp but has not yet returned to practice."Ahmad is working his rear end off," Drinkwitz said. "He's doing everything we can ask him to do, but (he's) just not going to be able to be ready for that first game."Drinkwitz also provided more clarity on what still needs to happen before Hardy can return to live action, saying Hardy must complete two full weeks of practice at full speed before Missouri would consider putting him in a game. 

        
            
                College football's best coaching matchups of 2026: Marcus Freeman vs. Mario Cristobal leads top 10
                
                    Brad Crawford                
            
                            
    
                
                    
    
Hardy has not reached that point, meaning that two-week ramp-up period has yet to begin. That leaves the timing of his return uncertain."Does that mean mid-September? I don't know. Does it mean mid-October? I don't know," Drinkwitz said. "I need a two-week, fully invested, be-able-to-practice-at-full-speed, before we consider playing in the game, and I'm not there yet."Missouri plays at Kansas on Sept. 11 and hosts Troy on Sept. 19 before opening SEC play at Mississippi State on Sept. 26.
Clear as mudDrinkwitz's announcement at SEC Media Days in July that Hardy had been "medically cleared" did not mean he was ready to return to football activities. It meant he could begin the next phase of his rehabilitation.At the time, Drinkwitz said the return-to-football process could take five-to-eight weeks. Saturday marked five weeks since that process began.Hardy was shot in the upper leg at a concert in Mississippi in May and required emergency surgery. Drinkwitz said in July that the bullet struck a bone, which has complicated the recovery.
Roberts takes over in the meantimeMissouri will turn to senior Jamal Roberts as its primary running back while Hardy remains sidelined.Roberts rushed for 753 yards and six touchdowns last season. He has averaged 5.5 yards per carry in his three years at Missouri, while Hardy has averaged 6.0 in his career, and both backs posted an identical 11.3% explosive-run rate.Missouri also added transfers Xai'Shaun Edwards and Malae Fonoti to the running back room.
Still, Hardy's absence leaves a significant hole.The Mississippi native was one of the nation's best players at his position last season after rushing for 1,649 yards and 16 touchdowns. He was a consensus All-American, a Doak Walker Award finalist and the SEC's leading rusher.Roberts now gets the first opportunity to replace that production, at least until Hardy is ready."Jamal's been phenomenal," Drinkwitz said. "He was voted a captain by his teammates yesterday. He's responded the right way. He's had an excellent camp."

title: College basketball transfer portal 5-for-5 tracker: Grading each move in new free agency window - CBS Sports
description: The moniker "National Championships are won in April but are built in the spring" rings a bit hollow in a college basketball offseason t
body:
The moniker "National Championships are won in April but are built in the spring" rings a bit hollow in a college basketball offseason that may never end. A slew of fifth-year seniors have brazenly challenged the NCAA for an extra year of eligibility, and it's changing the complexion of teams just a few weeks before first official practices tip off in late September.Michigan State transfer Jaxon Kohler committed to BYU on Thursday, filling Kevin Young's biggest hole on the roster at the final hour. Kohler averaged 12.6 points and 8.9 rebounds while shooting 39% from 3-point range for a Michigan State club that earned a No. 3 seed in the 2026 NCAA Tournament. Kohler signed an Exhibit 10 contract and suited up for the Utah Jazz's summer league team, but he has a pathway to return to college basketball after winning a temporary restraining order against the NCAA.The chaos continued on Friday when former UCLA guard Donovan Dent committed to LSU, marking just the latest player who may or may not be eligible for the 2026-27 season to commit to play for first-year coach Will Wade. Dent will join his former UCLA teammate, Skyy Clark, in Baton Rouge if they're eligible to play.And for a Saturday night news dump? Former Missouri star Mark Mitchell transferred to Kentucky, solidifying Mark Pope's squad as the top-ranked transfer portal class in the 247Sports rankings.
The NCAA adopted new age-based eligibility guidelines -- dubbed five-in-five -- in June but chose not to grandfather in the Class of 2022 for a fifth year of eligibility. Kohler is one of hundreds of seniors in over double-digit court cases who have disputed the NCAA's new rule. Even with numerous losses in court cases in Colorado, California, Tennessee, Georgia and Ohio, the NCAA has held firm that it will not budge. So, the judicial system will have the final verdict, and the outlook for dozens of contenders will hinge on it.
        
            
                Candid Coaches: Who will be the best college hoops team in 2026-27? Florida, Duke, Tennessee lead the way
                
                    Matt Norlander                
            
                            
    
                
                    
    
As of now, the Big 12 is shaping up to be a major winner after a handful of victories in court cases have cleared the way for fifth-year seniors to return back to college ball. Texas Tech, Cincinnati, BYU, West Virginia, Oklahoma State, Arizona and Houston have all landed legitimate starters or rotation players from the fifth-year market. Kohler is the 12th fifth-year senior to commit to a Big 12 team in the last month. The SEC is second amongst high-majors with six fifth-year seniors currently committed.
Let's dive into how the most notable names will impact their respective clubs.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Kentucky -- Mark MitchellFormer school: MissouriInstant analysis: Pope has been under a microscope this offseason after Kentucky's second-round exit in the NCAA Tournament. The Wildcats had a very high-priced roster last season, and with the talent Kentucky has landed, the roster's cost is shaping up to be among the highest in the sport. Mitchell is a terrific add for Kentucky, assuming he's eligible. The fit next to Milan Momcilovic and Malachi Moreno in the frontcourt will be one to watch. You can argue that Mitchell is the best player who is seeking an additional year of eligibility, so Kentucky landing him is a massive win. On the flip side, the pressure is really, really going to be on Pope to get this right. The Wildcats have the talent on paper to compete for a Final Four berth. Anything less would cause for a revolution next offseason. Grade: A -- Cameron Salerno
        
            
                Mark Mitchell transferring to Kentucky: Wildcats land former Missouri big man after court allows fifth season
                
                    Matt Norlander                
            
                            
    
                
                    
    

                            
    
                                                
                    
    LSU -- Donovan DentFormer school: UCLAInstant analysis: LSU's a bold strategy this offseason of recruiting as many players as possible who may not be eligible for the 2026-27 season is something that will either be genius or backfire. I don't think there will be an in-between. Dent is one of the best seniors fighting for an extra year of eligibility available, so it makes sense why LSU would at least try. One suitor that made a ton of sense for Dent before the dust settled was Gonzaga, but LSU could have some major holes on its roster if players aren't given a fifth year of eligibility. Dent is one of the best passers in the sport and would raise the floor of this roster immediately, which is trying to make noise in Year 1 of Will Wade's tenure. It's hard to picture how this will play out when the season starts in November. However, the bottom line is adding a player of Dent's caliber during late August is unheard of. Grade: A- -- Salerno

                            
    
                                                
                    
    BYU -- Jaxon KohlerFormer school: Michigan StateInstant analysis: You could make a strong case that Kohler was the best fifth-year senior on the board. His fit with BYU is almost perfect. BYU needed rebounding in the worst way. Kohler is an insatiable rebounder who rated in the 96th percentile in defensive rebounding and the 85th percentile in offensive rebounding. That'll play. BYU also needed a pick-and-pop big man to keep the paint open for point guard Rob Wright, who is a rim-pressure machine. Kohler can hold up that end of the bargain as well. Kohler splashed 58 3-pointers for MSU last season.He also provides a maniac competitor, who should be a fan favorite in Provo from the jump. Kohler can play the 4 or the 5 for this Cougs' club, which gives Kevin Young plenty of lineup versatility. BYU can lean offense with a five-man lineup of Wright, Collin Chandler, five-star freshman Bruce Branch, Tyler Betsey and Kohler. That's five shooters. Or BYU can go with a double-big lineup with Kohler at the 4 next to Polish big man Jakub Urbaniak. You'll also see some lineups with Kohler paired next to hyper-energetic, uber-athletic forward Khadim Mboup.With Kohler in the mix, BYU has elevated from an NCAA Tournament-caliber team into a true Big 12 contender. Grade: A -- Isaac Trotter

                            
    
                                                
                    
    Oklahoma -- BJ Edwards & Duke BrennanFormer schools: SMU and Villanova, respectivelyInstant analysis: The Sooners have done yeoman's work in the fifth-year senior market. Edwards and Brennan both project to be Day One starters for Porter Moser. Edwards was one of SMU's most valuable players, and the Ponies missed him dearly in its late-season collapse. The 6-foot-3 guard is an excellent defender who chips in with creation, shot-making and rim pressure. He just does a lot of things well. Brennan, meanwhile, is a major shot in the arm for OU's frontcourt. He is slated to start at center after averaging 12.4 points and 10.3 rebounds for Villanova this past season. While he's not an elite rim protector, Brennan has a ton of utility because he can pass and is always in the right place at the right time on defense. Oh, and he's tough.Oklahoma looks every bit the part of a dangerous NCAA Tournament team with Brennan and Edwards teaming up with star point guard Xzayvier Brown and returning forward Derrion Reid to form a legit nucleus of veteran difference-makers. Grade: A -- Isaac Trotter

                            
    
                                                
                    
    UNLV -- AJ StorrFormer school: Ole MissInstant analysis: Storr is one of the most well-traveled players in college basketball and will play for his fifth different school in the last five seasons if he suits up for UNLV. After stops at St. John's, Wisconsin and Kansas, Storr had an up-and-down season at Ole Miss under Chris Beard. Storr can be an impactful player in the right situation, but the fit is everything.  Grade: B- -- Salerno
                            
    
                                                
                    
     Louisville -- Seth Trimble Former school: North CarolinaInstant analysis: This is all about fortifying Louisville's defense. With Trimble in tow, Louisville has an elite point-of-attack defender to pair with big man Flory Bidunga, who will be on the short list for National Defensive Player of the Year. Trimble is an excellent athlete who can take the toughest assignments every single night. When Louisville plays Duke, Trimble will guard John Blackwell. When Louisville plays Miami, Trimble will shadow Acaden Lewis. You get the point. Trimble is also physical enough to switch up the lineup onto bigger wings or forwards, giving Louisville's staff some extra defensive versatility from a scheme perspective.  There's meat on the bone offensively, too. Trimble won't ever be a high-volume 3-point shooter, but he's an elite transition scorer joining a scheme that wants to score a ton in transition. Trimble won't be a star, but he can impact winning with his defense, rim pressure, turbo transition scoring and knack for getting to the foul line.  
Trimble will compete with Adrian Wooley and De'Shayne Montgomery to start at the 2, but don't be surprised if Louisville explores starting Wooley and Trimble if Arkansas transfer wing Karter Knox isn't up to snuff. Louisville has spent an exorbitant amount of money on this roster. It's time to win. Grade: B+ -- Isaac Trotter
                            
    
                                                
                    
    LSU -- Skyy ClarkFormer school: UCLAInstant analysis: LSU has only four (eligible) players on its roster with less than three months until the 2026-27 season begins. So, what's the solution for first-year coach Will Wade? Recruit more players who have eligibility in limbo. Clark will need a waiver to play a fifth season. If he's eligible, he will add shooting, defense and a lot of college experience to LSU's roster. Wade's roster building this summer has certainly been a major question mark and storyline. If some or most of the players he recruited are ruled eligible, then LSU will be able to compete in the SEC. If they're not, well, it could get ugly. Grade: B -- Salerno

                            
    
                                                
                    
     Texas Tech -- Darrion Williams Former school: NC State Instant analysis: We all know how this is going to go because we've seen it work at such a high level. Darrion Williams became the best version of himself in Lubbock, helping Texas Tech make the Elite Eight in 2025, and that's the expectation in his reunion. The Red Raiders have an extremely potent offensive ceiling with Williams in the mix. His ability to mismatch hunt, draw two defenders and spray it to snipers like Cruz Davis, DaKari Spear or Dra Gibbs-Lawhorn should give Texas Tech some easy buttons to press offensively while All-American big man JT Toppin heals up from a torn ACL. But there were also times last year at NC State where Williams looked lethargic and disinterested. That won't fly for McCasland, whose secret sauce may be how he draws out a different level of competitive fire from his club. You will compete, or you won't play. Williams looks poised to be a 15-point, five-rebound, three-assist guy for a Texas Tech team that will be among the Big 12's best once March rolls around. Grade: A+ -- Isaac Trotter 
                            
    
                                                
                    
     Arizona -- RJ Godfrey Former school: ClemsonInstant analysis: Are you allowed to play for Arizona without being a weight-room warrior? Godfrey, a chiseled 6-foot-7, 240-pound forward from Clemson, will give this Arizona front line some serious thump. Arizona just battered teams last year with physicality from Koa Peat and Tobe Awaka. Godfrey can supply some of that. He's not a shooter (8-for-37 from 3-point range in his career), but he knows that his bread is buttered in the paint. He'll be an impactful rebounder, defender and secondary playmaker. Godfrey just impacts winning and projects to be a Day One starter for Arizona. Grade: A -- Isaac Trotter

                            
    
                                                
                    
     Syracuse -- Amarri Monroe Former school: Quinnipiac Instant analysis: Monroe was on high-major radars a year ago at this time before exiting the portal to return to Quinnipiac for his senior season. He was one of the elite mid-major prospects with a combination of positional size and skill that is extremely tantalizing.  At 6-foot-7 and 230 pounds, Monroe will have no problem adjusting to the size and speed at the high-major ranks. Monroe won't average 15-and-8 at Syracuse, but he'll help Gerry McNamara's club as a high-feel role player. Monroe just blends into any roster because he impacts the game in a ton of different ways. He can cut. He can post mismatches. He can knock down a jumper. He can make plays for others. He can guard three or four positions. Monroe also fits into the ethos of Syracuse's new supersized roster. 11 of Syracuse's top-12 players will be 6-foot-5 or taller. This looks like another no-doubt rotation player, but I'd expect Monroe's defense to be ahead of the offense for a minute. Grade: B -- Isaac Trotter 
                            
    
                                                
                    
     Houston -- Chendall Weaver Former school: TexasInstant analysis: Weaver is one of the elite offensive-rebounding guards in college basketball. Do you need to hear anything else about his fit with Houston? That alone should curry favor with a Houston coaching staff that prioritizes rebounding more than anything else in basketball. Weaver's motor is always revving. His athleticism and court coverage will also be a valuable asset for a Houston defense that traps, rotates and swarms everywhere. Grade: B -- Isaac Trotter 

                            
    
                                                
                    
     Cincinnati -- MJ Collins Former school: Utah State Instant analysis: There's comfort in familiarity. Collins turned into the best version of himself (17.5 points, 36% from 3-point range) under Jerrod Calhoun at Utah State. Following his coach to Cincinnati should be a wise decision. Collins was one of the best athletes in a down Mountain West last year. He won't be able to overwhelm opposing guards quite as easily in the Big 12, but the 6-foot-4 guard is a capable shot-maker who is excellent in transition, moves without the basketball well and does not turn it over. Cincinnati has a lot of good players on this team, but Collins may have the best case for All-Big 12 honors. Grade: A -- Isaac Trotter 
                            
    
                                                
                    
     Tennessee -- Jalen Washington Former school: VanderbiltInstant analysis: Tennessee's frontcourt desperately needed another body to fortify this group. Washington provides Rick Barnes with a chance to tap into some five-out lineups, but he can also play alongside DeWayne Brown or Miles Rubin in a Twin Towers look. Washington should have a path to play at least 18 minutes a night, and he's an upgrade over VCU transfer Christian Fermin. While the 3-ball has never become a huge part of his arsenal, Washington should provide a serviceable target in the pick-and-roll game for Tennessee's talented backcourt. He rated in the 84th percentile as a roller in pick-and-rolls last year, although Tyler Tanner has a ton to do with that. Most importantly, Tennessee now has three playable big men it can cycle in and out as Barnes sees fit. That's key after losing Jaylen Carey, JP Estrella, Cade Phillips and Felix Okpara to the portal or graduation. Grade: B -- Isaac Trotter 
                            
    
                                                
                    
     Gonzaga -- Javon Bennett Former school: DaytonInstant analysis: Bennett is a bit undersized at 5-10, but a supersized Gonzaga roster can cover up those gaps. Bennett, in return, can provide plenty of utility because he has a strap and rarely turns it over. Bennett shot 39% on 153 catch-and-shoot 3s last season for Dayton, and he is a very capable pull-up shooter as well. You can't go under pick-and-rolls when Bennett is involved in the action. Grade: B+ -- Isaac Trotter 
                            
    
                                                
                    
     North Carolina -- Cameron Fens Former school: South Dakota Instant analysis: Fens adds a different look to North Carolina's frontcourt. The burly 7-footer averaged 14.4 points and 8.7 rebounds in the Summit League last year. His offensive rebounding and wide screens should be useful for a UNC frontcourt that was a little light in the britches. But the defensive concerns are very real. Fens struggles to guard in space, and he will get picked on defensively in pick-and-rolls. Fens is not a problem-solver on that end for UNC, but he can be a serviceable rotation player. Grade: C -- Isaac Trotter

description: Watson clearly took the booing to heart
body:
Watson clearly took the booing to heart
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Aug 22, 2026

    7:05 pm ET

            4 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        While his performance against the Bills did not help his cause in his position battle against Shedeur Sanders, Deshaun Watson likely hurt it even more during his postgame press conference while addressing being booed by Browns fans. Watson, after going 5 of 12 for 36 yards and an interception during Cleveland's 31-7 loss to the Bills, decided to go on the offensive when asked about the boos. "I think the whole world knows it has nothing to do about the performance," Watson said. "It's a little bit more personal than that. So, I think it's a disrespectful thing."To make his point, Watson noted that Saturday wasn't the first time that he felt the ire of Browns fans. He added that he gets treated better by opposing fans. 
 "Last time I played on this field, I tore my Achilles. That same fan base, they cheered when I got hurt," he said. "What does that have to do with anything about performance? When a person gets hurt, especially in your home stadium, and they cheer."Watson said that his experiences with Browns fans are usually only negative on either social media or during home games. He was hoping that the situation regarding the fans' treatment of him would be better given his involvement in the city and after he worked to get himself back in position to compete to be the Browns' starting quarterback. "I thought being away for two years and working myself back from two Achilles injuries and putting the time in and being around the facility, being around the city, doing charity work in the city, supporting the Cleveland Browns, hanging out with fans whenever I do see them, being honest, being the type of person that I know I am and the character would help," he said. "And I guess it hasn't. So that's why I say it's personal. So it is what it is. People have their own opinions. There's only so much you can do to change that. So at the end of the day, I just have to continue to just work on it and strive to be better mentally moving forward."  
Saturday was a continuation of the downward spiral that has been Watson's career, especially since he arrived in Cleveland in 2022. A three-time Pro Bowler with the Texans, injuries and inconsistent play have plagued Watson throughout his time with the Browns. He is 9-10 as the Browns' starting quarterback with just 19 touchdowns, 12 interceptions and a mediocre 61.2% completion percentage. Adding to the frustration that has been Watson's story in Cleveland is the amount of capital the Browns spent to get him. They sent Houston six draft picks that included three consecutive first-round picks in addition to signing Watson to a record-setting, five-year, $230 million fully guaranteed contract. It's undeniably one of -- if not the -- worst transactions in the history of sports.  There's also the fact that the Browns traded for Watson despite the fact that he had already been sued by over two dozen female massage therapists for sexual harassment and sexual assault (in 2022, it was announced that 20 of the 24 women who sued Watson had reached confidential settlements). Watson's time in Cleveland began with him serving an 11-game suspension for violating the league's personal conduct policy. 
In addition to Watson's plight, the fact that he's competing against the immensely popular Sanders doesn't help his cause. Sanders, who made the Pro Bowl as a rookie, went 9 of 11 for 74 yards with a touchdown and an interception against the Bills. Sanders also shined during his postgame press conference when he was asked about the fans' treatment of Watson. "I think we all need to understand that we're all human," he said. "I don't really do things to humans I wouldn't want done to me. ... Just for our fans, I appreciate y'all showing up and everything. However y'all feel about the situation, about Deshaun, I think it's more about a bigger purpose than just respect. The respect thing that I feel like should be there. Because we're out trying to do our best and trying to serve the franchise the best way possible. We're going out there every game and doing everything we can do. I don't really appreciate that." As noted above, Watson didn't do himself any favors both during and after Saturday's game. And while it appears that his time in Cleveland is destined to be remembered as an epic disappointment, Watson remains optimistic that there is light at the end of the tunnel in terms of his playing career. 
"I don't regret anything in my life," he said. "I think the Lord puts you in situations for a reason. I don't regret anything at all. I had different thoughts on how it was gonna be, but it is what it is. Sometimes, the tables turn, and I'm patient enough -- because I'm a child of God -- to wait for that change. So, I ain't tripping."

title: Zolani Tete dies at 38: Former world champion found dead after shooting in South Africa - CBS Sports
description: Tete held titles at junior bantamweight and bantamweight in his 34-fight pro career
body:
Tete held titles at junior bantamweight and bantamweight in his 34-fight pro career
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Aug 22, 2026
                            
                    at
    7:45 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            1 min read
            
        
    

            
    
Zolani Tete, a former two-division world champion, is dead at 38 following a shooting outside his home in Mdantsane, South Africa. The South African Department of Sport confirmed Tete's death Friday night.Tete started his professional career 13-0 before receiving his first shot at world championship gold. Tete lost that first championship opportunity when he was stopped by fellow South African Moruti Mthalane in their IBF flyweight title bout.After the loss to Mthalane, Tete went just 3-2 before a 12-fight winning streak launched him into the ranks of boxing's best and most exciting fighters.During that streak, Tete took a decision win over Teiru Kinoshita to capture the IBF junior bantamweight championship. He made one successful defense of that title, a knockout of Paul Butler, before vacating the title rather than face a mandatory challenger.Tete eventually moved to bantamweight, where he went on to defeat Arthur Villanueva for the interim WBO championship. He would then be elevated to full champion, where he made his first defense of the title against Siboniso Gonya. Tete knocked out Gonya with his first punch of the fight, setting a record for the fastest knockout in a title fight in boxing history.Tete made two more defense of the belt before suffering an upset third-round knockout loss to John Riel Casimero.Tete bounced back with two wins, but tested positive for performance enhancing drugs in the second of those fights. He was subsequently suspended for four years, a period that ended just weeks before his murder.

body:
The Blaugrana are yet to replace Robert Lewandowski, with not long to go before the end of the summer transfer window

    9:14 am ET

        The 2026-2027 LaLiga season kicked off around Spain and Hansi Flick's Barcelona are the current Spanish title holders. After claiming the domestic league the past two seasons since the German manager took over the Catalan side, the main target of the former Bayern Munich head coach is to improve the team's performance in Europe. In his first season, Barcelona were eliminated by Inter in the semifinals of the Champions League, while last season they were knocked out by Spanish side Atletico Madrid in the quarterfinals. With those setbacks in mind, can we expect more from Barcelona in the upcoming European campaign? However, they are still yet to sign their starting center striker, which remains a key area to address.The Blaugrana made some changes in their roster in the first part of the summer transfer window but so far have failed to replace their starting striker, Robert Lewandowski, who left as a free agent and joined MLS side Chicago Fire this summer. With not long to go before the end of the transfer session, Barcelona president Joan Laporta and sporting director Deco are still working to find the right player for their attacking squad. The main question heading into the new season is, can Barcelona achieve greater success in Europe despite still failing to sign a proven central striker?Watch Barcelona all season long in the UEFA Champions League live on Paramount+.Arrivals: Rodri, attacking help but no strikerBarcelona made some big signings ahead of the summer, as Anthony Gordon joined from Newcastle for around $80 million and Karim Adeyemi joined from Borussia Dortmund for around $20 million. These signings strengthen Flick's options on the wings, allowing him to rotate his players more effectively between league and cup competitions, especially with Ferran Torres now at PSG and Marcus Rashford's loan move ending. However, the signing of Rodri was arguably the most important addition. The captain of the Spanish national team, who lifted the 2026 World Cup, is widely regarded as one of the best players in the world, especially after winning the 2024 Ballon d'Or. Rodri ultimately decided to join Barcelona despite also holding talks with Real Madrid, something that was also confirmed by Jose Mourinho. 

        
            
                Why signing World Cup winner Rodri may be what sees Barcelona end Champions League drought
                
                    Chuck Booth                
            
                            
    
                
                    
    
During the recent exclusive interview with El Chiringuito, Mourinho claimed he "had doubts" about Rodri after speaking with him."I spoke with him a couple of times. Real Madrid made him a very good offer. I think the relationship between Real Madrid and City is very good. The club made him a generous offer. Rodri had doubts, he doubted, and I think what happened is that the doubts Rodri had gave me doubts. He's an extraordinary player. But I think Real Madrid are so big that we can't have players who think twice. That's the concept. But he behaved properly with us, and I wish him well," Mourinho said.With Lewandowski leaving ahead of the summer, Barcelona failed to sign a proper replacement with less than 10 days left before the end of the summer transfer window. The Catalan club tried to sign Julian Alvarez from Atletico Madrid, but the Spanish side blocked the move despite the Argentine striker pushing for a transfer to Flick's team. The two clubs then became embroiled in a verbal war that grew increasingly tense during the first weeks of June. Since then, they have been unable to find a way to sit down and reach an agreement. Barcelona seemed a bit stuck and didn't find a proper alternative yet. In recent days, Inter captain Lautaro Martinez emerged as a candidate according to multiple Spanish reports, but Inter president Giuseppe Marotta, speaking to DAZN, cooled the rumors down ahead of the opening match of the season against Monza.
"Lautaro is our captain, our history. There are not even the conditions to sell him. You should not even speak about Lautaro's exit," he said. The next target: Winning outside Spain When Flick was called by Laporta to become the new Barcelona coach, the target was clear -- winning the Champions League. In his first two years in charge, Flick has achieved his domestic objectives, leading Barcelona to two titles in two seasons. The next step is to make their mark in Europe, and this is where the signings of Rodri, Gordon and Adeyemi could prove crucial, adding more talent to a roster that also sees players such as Lamine Yamal, Raphinha and more lead the charge.Winning in Europe is different. Success can depend heavily on the form of key players at specific moments of the season, as last season proved. However, trying to compete without a proper replacement for Lewandowski would be a risky decision that is unlikely to pay off. That is why signing a top-class central striker in the coming days must be a priority for the Blaugrana ahead of the new season. This is especially true given Real Madrid's summer additions, which could make the domestic race even more challenging and leave Barcelona with little space for mistakes in key matches.

title: NFL preseason Week 2 winners and losers: Bo Nix shines in return, Deshaun Watson takes shot at Browns fans - CBS Sports
description: The second week of the NFL preseason is underway, with the regular season drawing ever closer. Preseason football is like a box of choco
body:
The second week of the NFL preseason is underway, with the regular season drawing ever closer. Preseason football is like a box of chocolates as Forrest Gump would say, "You never know what you're going to get." That's because some squads have their starters chained to the bench, some play minimal snaps and some could receive as much of a half of work. Observing who could emerge as a real contributor from the chaos that is preseason football is tricky given the varying degrees of skill levels on the field all at the same time, but it's possible to identify who maximized their opportunity and who would like a do-over. Let's kick identify the winners and losers of Week 2 of the 2026 preseason.Winners
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Shedeur SandersWas Shedeur Sanders perfect in his preseason Week 2 start? Hardly. Was he much, much better than Deshaun Watson? Absolutely. (Though the bar was basically on the ground).Sanders came out firing after having to wait out a weather delay of nearly an hour, connecting on all four of his passes on the opening drive. That included a fourth-down conversion to tight end Blake Whiteheart and, later on, an 8-yard touchdown pass to Luke Floriea. Sanders had a few of Cleveland's starters -- namely rookies Spencer Fano and Denzel Boston -- out there with him, but he was mostly working with backups. The Bills rested basically all of their starters, too.
"There's a lot there to like," coach Todd Monken said. "I mean he plays with a certain amount of confidence. He has gotten a lot better at getting rid of the ball. Certainly he wants to make a play."... I thought he did a lot of really good things. I'm really proud of him and where he's come from. From the moment I got here until now, very impressive."Monken in specific cited the above touchdown pass and a 23-yard completion on third and 15 as two of Sanders' best moments.
Sanders actually hit on his first eight passes in a row before an interception in which he threw slightly behind Jermaine Terry II. Monken said the ball "certainly" could have been caught. It also could have been a better throw.
Overall, it was a strong day for Sanders -- 9-for-11, 74 yards, one touchdown, one interception, one sack -- and a much better outing than in Week 1.
        
            
                Browns quarterback battle: Shedeur Sanders decent in start, Deshaun Watson struggles, both throw interceptions
                
                    Zachary Pereles                
            
                            
    
                
                    
    

                            
    
                                                
                    
    Falcons vibesPreseason scores do not matter at all, but there might not have been a single team needing a good week more than the Falcons. Atlanta got walloped by Denver, 27-7, last week, hours after the news came out that James Pearce Jr. was suspended eight games. Tua Tagovailoa looked awful, the defense looked awful, and the vibes were bad.
Week 2 was much better. With no Tagovailoa or Michael Penix Jr. playing, Cooper Rush and Jack Strand both played well, and three different players had a rushing touchdown in a 34-6 win over the Colts.The best news, however, came after the game: Kevin Stefanski said Penix has been cleared to return to 11-on-11 work after a lengthy rehabilitation from yet another torn ACL. Maybe Tagovailoa is already the de-facto starter since it's taken Penix a bit, but it's always nice to get positive injury updates.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    De'Zaun Stribling San Francisco 49ers 2026 second-round pick wide receiver De'Zhaun Stribling, the rookie 33rd overall pick out of Ole Miss, is THE breakout star of the preseason this year. After catching four of his five targets for 46 yards receiving on Thursday against the Los Angeles Chargers, Stribling is now up to 11 catches for 109 yards receiving on 13 targets. That makes Stribling the first player since at least 2017 to produce at least 11 catches combined within the first 20 minutes of two consecutive preseason games, per CBS Sports Research. Many preseason All-Stars don't end up contributing much outside of special teams for their respective squads, but it's safe to say Stribling will have a place on head coach Kyle Shanahan's play call sheet early this regular season. That's especially true when factoring in how snake-bitten by injury San Francisco is at the position.

                            
    
                                                
                    
    The Houston Texans defenseNo, Will Anderson Jr., Danielle Hunter, Derek Stingley Jr. and the rest of the starters from the NFL's No. 1 total defense (277.2 total yards per game allowed) in 2025 weren't on the field Thursday night, but the Houston Texans' ferocious tenacity on defense certainly was. They bullied Las Vegas Raiders first overall pick rookie quarterback Fernando Mendoza in the first half, generating an 80-yard pick six by fourth-round rookie linebacker Wade Woodaz and an 11-yard sack by second-round rookie defensive tackle Kayden McDonald. 
Seeing McDonald flash pass rush chops like this should send shivers down the spines of offensive coordinators all around the league. If there was an area Houston needed to shore up on their defense, it was defensive tackle, and they were able to do so by drafting McDonald, the 2026 NFL Draft's top defensive tackle prospect in the eyes of many, including yours truly. McDonald, who is listed at 6-foot-3-inches tall while weighing 326 pounds, was more of a run stuffer than a pass rusher in college at Ohio State, but if he can find his groove early on when tasked to get after the quarterback, Houston's defense could be a much greater problem for the rest of the league. 

                            
    
                                                
                    
    Jermod McCoy Tennessee All-SEC cornerback Jermod McCoy profiled as a likely first-round pick in the 2026 NFL Draft until the medicals surrounding his knee scared teams away. McCoy did suffer a torn ACL in January 2025, but fears about inflammation and arthritis in his knee caused him to tumble all the way down to being the 101st overall pick and a fourth-round draft choice. In the Raiders' 22-20 preseason victory over the Texans on Thursday, McCoy appeared to be moving well and in phase with opposing wide receivers when tasked with dropping back into man coverage. Perhaps he can end up becoming the best value pick of the 2026 rookie draft class if given the opportunity to receive snaps with Las Vegas' starting defense. 

                            
    
                                                
                    
    Geno SmithOutside of Minnesota Vikings quarterback J.J. McCarthy, perhaps no other quarterback had a more depressing 2025 season than Geno Smith. The two-time Pro Bowler led the NFL in both sacks taken (55) and interceptions thrown (17) last season while attempting to pilot then-offensive coordinator Chip Kelly's scheme with the Las Vegas Raiders. Those statistics made Smith just the sixth quarterback since the 1970 AFL/NFL merger to lead the NFL in both sacks and interceptions in the same season. Kelly had to trudge back down to the college ranks, where he is now Northwestern's offensive coordinator. 
Smith, a second-round pick of the New York Jets in the 2013 NFL Draft, returned to New York after the Jets acquired him and a 2026 seventh-round pick from the Raiders in exchange for a 2026 sixth-round pick. He kicked off his second stint with the Jets with a perfect drive while leading the Jets' starting lineup on the opening possession against the Pittsburgh Steelers on Friday before head coach Aaron Glenn decided he'd seen enough from the 35-year-old veteran quarterback to end his night. Smith completed all seven of his throws on New York's opening drive, including the 13-yard scoring strike to tight end Jelani Woods. He also connected with both of the Jets' top wide receivers, Garrett Wilson (one catch on one target for 10 yards) and Adonai Mitchell (two catches on two targets for 29 yards), to finish the night with 65 yards passing. Perhaps Smith's 2025 season was more a product of the overall ineptitude of Kelly's and Pete Caroll's offensive coaching staff. Carroll was given the boot after just one season in Las Vegas, after all. 

                            
    
                                                
                    
    New York Jets defenseThe 2025 New York Jets became the first team in NFL history to finish a season with zero interceptions in a regular season. That dry spell unofficially ended in Week 2 of the preseason. Safety Andre Cisco jumped Pittsburgh Steelers quarterback Will Howard's throw to wide receiver Roman Wilson for the takeaway. 
Jets cornerback Samuel Womack III, a 27-year-old journeyman, generated New York's second takeaway of the night on another interception of Howard. Safe to say New York is an exponentially better ball-hawking group than their 2025 squad. 

                            
    
                                                
                    
    Bo NixThe last time Denver Broncos quarterback Bo Nix was on a football field, he was fresh off breaking his ankle in an overtime victory over the Buffalo Bills in the AFC divisional round. He returned to action in Week 2 of the preseason and thrived in his two drives, helping generate 10 points for Denver. Nix connected with new No. 1 target Jaylen Waddle up the seam, and the former Miami Dolphins speedster blew by Green Bay Packers All-Pro safety Xavier McKinney for a gain of 35 yards. That's the big play threat Denver sorely lacked in 2025. 
He then capped the drive by lofting a pinpoint pass to running back RJ Harvey on a wheel route down the right sideline for the 21-yard touchdown toss. Denver head coach Sean Payton ended Nix's night after the Broncos drilled a 53-yard field goal at the conclusion of his second drive, so he finished with 76 yards passing and a touchdown on 6 of 9 passing. Not a bad way to shake the rust off after suffering a broken ankle. 

                            
    
                                                
                    
    Packers special teamsSpecial teams have been a bugaboo for Green Bay for the last several seasons since the Packers' all-time scoring leader, Mason Crosby, took over as the team's kicker following the conclusion of the 2022 season. The dark days at Green Bay's kicker position might be over thanks to sixth-round rookie Trey Smack. He drilled two 58-yard field goals in the first week of the preseason, one of which didn't count because of a defensive penalty. In Week 2 in Denver, he smacked, pun intended, a 51-yard kick, a 59-yard kick and a 43-yard kick through the uprights, the latter of which occurred as time expired in the first half. Green Bay All-Pro edge rusher Micah Parsons, who is still recovering from a torn ACL he suffered in Denver last season, is fired up about Smack's performance from the couch.
It wasn't just Smack showing out for the Packers' special teams unit. Veteran wide receiver Skyy Moore took the game's opening kickoff for 30 yards out to the Green Bay 37, and veteran running back Pierre Strong Jr. ripped off a 68-yard kickoff return down to Denver's 32. Looks like Packers new special teams coordinator Cam Achord has found an early groove in Green Bay. 

                            
    
                                                
                    
    Jonathan BrooksBrooks, who was the first running back drafted in the 2024 NFL Draft with the 46th overall pick in the second round by the Carolina Panthers, finally found the end zone in the NFL for the first time. Brooks tore his ACL in his final season at the University of Texas, and he missed the entire 2025 NFL season with another ACL tear he suffered in 2024. He is back in action this preseason, and Brooks was able to shimmy his way into the end zone from a yard out at the Jacksonville Jaguars.   
Losers
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Deshaun WatsonMaybe Deshaun Watson starts Week 1. Maybe he doesn't. What's clear, though, is that he is not an effective quarterback. Watson went 5-for-12 for 35 yards and an interception on a throw that simply cannot be made.
Watson was inaccurate, struggled at the first sign of pressure and made poor decisions. Browns fans who stuck out the rain delay booed him vociferously, a development Watson acknowledged went beyond his performance on the field."Last time I played on this field, I tore my Achilles, and that same fan base, they cheered when I got hurt," Watson said postgame. "What does that have to do with anything about performance? When a person get hurt, especially for your own city, and they cheer?"Watson said he doesn't regret coming to Cleveland -- "I don't regret anything in my life," he said -- but he admitted it hasn't gone the way he envisioned. That certainly includes Saturday's performance.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Commanders offenseDan Quinn said the Commanders' starting offense would play one series no matter what, but he certainly didn't want it to look like this: incompletion, sack, draw, punt. On Jayden Daniels' first snap, backup center Julian Good-Jones got beat, forcing a throw away. On the next snap, the top two tight ends -- Chig Okonkwo and John Bates -- both got beat, and Daniels had no chance.Offensive line is a significant concern, with center being at the top of that list: Projected starter Nick Allegretti is dealing with a calf issue. The depth across the board is questionable at best, too. The Commanders managed just 35 yards on 17 carries, a putrid 2.2-yard average.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    J.J. McCarthyWith the Vikings' starters resting, J.J. McCarthy got the start. It didn't go great for anyone involved, and it showed McCarthy's major flaws.The numbers on the surface aren't awful: 5-for-10 for 81 yards, one sack. Fifty of those 81 yards came on deep jump ball that Tai Felton happened to win; give McCarthy credit for avoiding the rush and giving his guy a chance here.But what happened thereafter gave us the full picture of where McCarthy is. On second-and-goal, he fired a ball too high for Felton in the back of the end zone. On fourth-and-goal, he missed a wide open Myles Price -- again, way, way too high -- in the front of the end zone. They're both throws that have to be made; the second one should be completed with his eyes closed. There were at least two other instances of McCarthy missing open guys, either high or wide (or both).McCarthy got beat up playing behind the backup offensive line, and that's a significant part of the rocky performance. He actually had an impressive third-and-14 completion that got called back due to penalty. But overall, there are too many misses, which is why McCarthy has gone from battling for the starting job to battling for the backup job.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Anthony Richardson and Riley LeonardSimilar to the McCarthy situation, Anthony Richardson has gone from high draft pick to injured, inconsistent starter to just trying to be the primary backup in short order. And Richardson didn't help his cause Saturday.Stats don't always tell the whole story. Richardson played behind a leaky (to put it nicely) offensive line, and his pass catchers didn't help him much, either. But 3-for-9, 24 yards with two sacks isn't pretty, no matter how you paint it. He did have this nice run.
Riley Leonard was pretty poor, too: 7-for-15 for 62 yards. The backup quarterback situation is pretty bleak. Don't lose Philip Rivers' phone number, I suppose.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Fernando MendozaFirst overall pick, rookie quarterback Fernando Mendoza had a couple of "Welcome to the NFL" moments on Thursday night against the smashmouth Houston Texans defense, tossing an 80-yard pick six and taking an 11-yard sack. He finished his night with just 86 yards, and the interception return touchdown thrown while completing 8 of his 15 passes. "It was a play action play, went through my progression, probably should've checked it down to the flat. I saw the flat player get over late to him," Mendoza told reporters when asked about his interception return touchdown thrown. "At that point, I started backing up and threw the check down to Mike Washington. It was not a good throw, we weren't on the same page and it was an interception."  Mendoza did have some nice moments, like a 22-yard dart to Raiders wide receiver Jalen Nailor in the middle of the field and just in between the Texans' zone defense. He wasn't asked to make a ton of those high-difficulty throws over the middle in college, but they are a staple of head coach Klint Kubiak's Shanahan-tree offense. Overall, Mendoza had a tough night at the office despite the occasional flash here and there. 
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Punter JK ScottSurrendering a punt return touchdown as a punter is never fun, but Los Angeles Chargers punter JK Scott earns a spot on this list for how he allowed San Francisco 49ers wide receiver Jacob Cowing to take his punt back 83 yards for the score. Scott had a chance to make a tackle on Cowing near the 49ers' 45-yard line, but instead of feigning any interest in bringing down San Francisco's return man, he sidesteps out of the way, almost appearing to hold the door open for him. When factoring in Scott will turn 31 years old on Oct. 30 during his ninth NFL season, it's understandable that he made a business decision in the preseason. However, he could have made it just a smidge less obvious, and in doing so, helped prevent a touchdown on special teams. 

                            
    
                                                
                    
    Will HowardThe 2025 New York Jets became the first squad in NFL history to finish a season with zero interceptions in a regular season. Pittsburgh Steelers quarterback Will Howard, the starter for the home team on Friday, acted as New York's slump buster, tossing not one but two picks the Jets' away on throws intended for wide receiver Roman Wilson over the middle of the field. Not a great way to stay ahead of third-round rookie Drew Allar on the depth chart. 
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Liam CoenCarolina Panthers head coach Dave Canales gave the NFL world a glimpse of his starters, giving quarterback Bryce Young and his starters two drives on Friday night. Jacksonville Jaguars head coach Liam Coen didn't meet the moment, keeping quarterback Trevor Lawrence and the rest of his starters in street clothes on the sidelines. Boring.

        Two of boxing's biggest -- and most unpredictable -- personalities will meet in the ring on Saturday when Rolando "Rolly" Romero defends his WBA welterweight championship against Teofimo Lopez Jr.Romero is something of an unexpected world champion, though he's accomplished the feat twice over in his career. Always a popular fighter based on his big personality and strong social media presence, Romero has never displayed elite boxing skills, instead relying on an offense-first style and solid power.In 2022, Romero received his first opportunity to break through to the top of the sport, but he was brutally stopped in the sixth round by Gervonta "Tank" Davis.In his next fight after losing to Davis, Romero won his first world championship, picking up a ninth-round TKO win over Ismael Barroso to capture the vacant WBA junior welterweight championship. That win was heavily tainted by the fact that Romero was getting thoroughly outclassed by Barroso, a late replacement in the fight, when the referee jumped in for a clear early stoppage nearly the second Romero had gathered any momentum.
Romero dropped the title in his next outing, getting stopped by Isaac "Pitbull" Cruz. Two fights later, Romero again found himself playing the "b-side" to a bigger name fighter when he took on Ryan Garcia in New York's Times Square.
        
            
                Teofimo Lopez Jr. looks to bounce back from disastrous loss when he faces Rolly Romero for welterweight title
                
                    Brian Campbell                
            
                            
    
                
                    
    
Garcia fought the worst fight of his life, turning in a lifeless performance that allowed Romero to win the "regular" WBA welterweight title, and was subsequently elevated to full champion when Jaron Ennis vacated his belt to move up in weight.Now, Romero faces Lopez, a fighter who has always been viewed as a man with elite talent but a lacking mental game, almost the inverse of Romero.
Lopez won the first 16 fights of his career, a run that culminated in a win over Richard Commey to claim the IBF lightweight championship and Vasiliy Lomachenko to add the WBA and WBO titles.Just as it seemed Lopez was poised to take over the sport, he suffered a devastating setback when he dropped a split decision to massive underdog George Kambosos Jr. Lopez was knocked down by Kambosos and clearly lost the fight, making the one card scored his way an oddity that seemed to convince Lopez boxing's elites had conspired against the bigger name fighter with the bigger fanbase and the bigger promoter in favor of a fighter largely unknown in the sport.As Lopez performed a backflip after the Kambosos loss, it confirmed to many that mental issues Lopez had displayed throughout his career -- along with a seemingly unhealthy attachment to his father serving as his trainer -- may hold him back from his true potential.
Lopez rebounded with six wins of varying quality, including struggles against Sandor Martín and Jamaine Ortiz, and a few impressive wins, including over Josh Taylor to capture the WBO junior welterweight title.That run brought Lopez to his most recent fight, where he was badly outclassed by Shakur Stevenson over 12 rounds. Lopez was nearly shut out that night, losing 119-109 on all three official scorecards.Against Stevenson, Teofimo Lopez Sr. offered little constructive advice in the corner, something that Lopez Jr. has taken issue with in the months since the loss, continuing their tumultuous relationship.
"I'm fighting a big puncher at 147 and going up to that weight for the first time," Lopez said at a recent media workout. "We're taking a risk, because it's no risk, no reward. I'm just focusing on my objectives so I can come out victorious."Every fight at 147 will be my biggest fight. I won't say they'll all be the most challenging. The best man will end up on top. Right now I'm only focused on Rolly Romero."Let's take a closer look at the rest of the undercard for Saturday night in Las Vegas with the latest odds from DraftKings before getting to a prediction and expert pick on the main event below.
Romero vs. Lopez fight card, oddsTeofimo Lopez Jr. -300 vs. Rolando Romero (c) +230, WBA welterweight titleYoenli Hernandez -1400 vs. Francisco Daniel Veron +750, middleweightsGary Antonio Russell -180 vs. Victor Santillan +140, junior featherweightsCarlos Utria -1600 vs. Israel Mercado +750, junior welterweightsMarco Romero -5000 vs. Kahlil Mitchell +1300, middleweightsBenjamin Johnson vs. Jose Gabriel Rodriguez, welterweightsJoseph Brown -5000 vs. Alton Wiggins +1300, junior middleweightsAldo Blancas -5000 vs. Ricky Mamone +1300, junior welterweightsWhere to watch Romero vs. Lopez Date: Saturday, Aug. 22 | Start time: 8 p.m. ET (Main card) (Main event ring walks expected around 11 p.m. ET)Location: T-Mobile Arena -- Las VegasTV Channel/Stream: DAZN PPV | Price: $79.99PredictionLopez is the better fighter. He's the man with more natural gifts. He's the fighter with more technical skills. However, Lopez is also a fighter with some obvious flaws. He's shown mental weakness and a tendency to get flustered the second things aren't coming easily in the ring. Lopez has also had extreme trouble with fighters who use movement and don't choose to engage. Sandor Martín took that approach in a fight where he likely deserved the decision, and that left Lopez asking "Do I still got it?" after the final bell.The problem for Romero is that he is very unlikely to be a fighter who is going to take a Martin-esque approach to fighting Lopez. Romero has a strong mental game, and that's a good tool against someone like Lopez, but he doesn't have the style to further fluster and beat Lopez unless he turns in a career-best performance.Romero beat Garcia because Garcia simply didn't show up that night in New York City. Garcia didn't engage and he didn't throw punches, making for an easy night for Romero. Lopez isn't likely to turn in a dud on that level, and all things being equal, it should be a fairly easy win for Lopez. Whether or not Lopez can score his first stoppage win since 2022 is a more intriguing question. Pick: Teofimo Lopez via UD

        Noche UFC finally has a new main event. A big featherweight showdown was scheduled between Yair Rodriguez and Jean Silva to headline the Sept. 12 event, but Rodriguez has been forced out of the bout with injury, leading to Jose Delgado's insertion.Delgado (12-2) has scored wins over Andre Fili and Austin Bashi thus far in 2026. Those wins have run Delgado's UFC record to 4-1 since he earned a UFC contract with a knockout of Ernie Juarez on "Dana White's Contender Series" in 2024. Delgado's lone UFC loss came to Nathaniel Wood by decision in October 2025, a fight for which Delgado missed weight.Silva sits at No. 6 in the UFC's media rankings. After winning his way into the UFC on Contender Series, Silva rattled off five consecutive wins in the Octagon, including four by knockout, before submitting Bryce Mitchell with an arm-triangle choke.
Silva suffered the first loss of his UFC career in 2025, when he was knocked out by a Diego Lopes spinning backfist in a thrilling UFC Fight Night main event.Silva rebounded from the Lopes loss by taking a hard-fought decision win over Arnold Allen at UFC 324, the first UFC event of the "Paramount Era."
